title: Emberwild – A Timing-Based Boss Raid RPG Built Around Dodging, Protection Switching and Gear Progression
author: Wrong-Month-4895
selftext:
Wanted to share a game I’ve been working on called **Emberwild**.

It’s a boss/raid RPG built around actually learning the fights. You move around the arena, dodge attacks, switch between melee/ranged/magic protection, manage food and tonics, use your special at the right time and gradually build your character through better equipment and upgrades.

**The video here is from an earlier version of the game.** The current build has already had quite a bit added since this footage, including a much bigger equipment system, actual gear/item icons, more loot and progression work, Forge changes, additional UI work and a lot of other improvements.

There are currently eight bosses, multiple difficulties, Boss Practice, a full raid, inventory and equipment, forging/upgrading, boss-specific rewards, legendary gear, progression, achievements and other permanent character systems.

It’s also gone quite a bit beyond being completely offline now. The current version has Discord sign-in, cloud saves, character names, shared high scores, a friends list and player presence.

You can play it here:

[https://camleto.itch.io/emberwilds](https://camleto.itch.io/emberwilds)

There’s also a downloadable Windows EXE version, which runs noticeably smoother on PC than playing it directly through the browser.

The biggest thing I’m working on now is moving the entire game into **Unity**.

The combat is already running there, and right now I’m moving the rest of the game across: the title screen, camp, equipment, inventory, Forge, Quartermaster, progression, saves and everything else before bringing all eight bosses and the complete raid over.

The reason for the Unity move is mostly where I want to take Emberwild next. I want to start learning more 3D modeling, build proper characters and bosses, improve the animations and attack effects, work on more custom music and generally have a lot more freedom with the visuals than I had with the original browser setup.

I’m keeping the existing game and mechanics intact while I move it over first instead of trying to remake everything at the same time.

Once the Unity version is caught up, that’s when I want to really start pushing the models, environments, animations and effects.

Eventually I want the Unity version to become the main version of Emberwild, with a proper Windows release, browser version and eventually a mobile/app release as well.

Still plenty left to do, but the game has changed a lot from what you can see in this video already.

Would love to hear what people think of the idea and especially what you’d want to see improved as it moves into Unity.
